pageCache.text:
Message from the Principal
I would like to extend a very warm welcome to Baylis Court School. I am honoured to lead the school as Principal, and proud to be part of the warm and welcoming community.
Baylis Court School is a comprehensive 11-18 school for girls, situated in Slough, Berkshire. There are 940 students on roll, including 140 students in the sixth form. Baylis Court is a community where each student is known and cared for, and their individual needs are met. Our school is a happy one where relationships between all members of the diverse community are overwhelmingly positive.

OPEN MORNINGS AND EVENING
OPEN MORNINGS AND EVENING
Come and see the school in action at one of our open mornings or meet the Principal and senior staff at our open evening.
Open mornings are on Mondays and Wednesdays in September and October starting at 9am.
You will be welcomed by our Principal, Mrs MacInnes, before taking a tour of our active classes with one of our knowledable and friendly pupils. Following this, there will be an opportunity for any questions to be answered by our Principal, SENCO and other key pastoral staff.
Please book your place here Open Morning bookings
Open Evening will be held on Tuesday 6 October, in the Arts Building at Baylis Court School. Mrs MacInnes will talk to you about the unique features of a Baylis Court education, and how our pupils embrace the values of kind, inquisitive and resilient. There will be time for questions and answers afterwards. There is no need to book, but if you'd like further information please contact us on 01753 531760 or bayliscourtschool@bayliscourt.slough.sch.uk

We look forward to seeing what these ‘Leaders of Tomorrow’ achieve in the future.

We are delighted to celebrate and share the success of our wonderful Year 11 pupils. We are incredibly proud of the commitment to their studies and the resilience they have shown throughout their GCSE courses.
The school’s mission, ‘Inspiring Leaders of Tomorrow’ underpins all that we do. Pupils are expected, encouraged and supported to achieve their very best academically. It is extremely pleasing to see so many pupils rise to the challenge and achieve outcomes that enable them to further their studies. All Year 11 pupils should be rightly proud of their achievements.
For individual pupils there are a wide range of success stories. It was a pleasure to celebrate with our pupils and their families on GCSE results day as the group of young people prepare for the next stage of their educational journey,
All pupils have been supported by our wonderful staff who have worked tirelessly, and with relentless enthusiasm. We are thrilled to celebrate the achievements of our incredible community.

pageCache.pageTitle: A Level Results Day - A Level Results Day - Latest News - Baylis Court School
pageCache.text:
A Level Results Day
Baylis Court School - Inspiring Leaders of Tomorrow
Students and staff at Baylis Court School came together today to mark A-level results day, celebrating the hard work, perseverance, and personal achievements of this year’s Sixth Form cohort.
The results mark the culmination of two years of dedication, with students successfully securing their chosen next steps across a diverse range of subjects including medicine, law, optometry, archaeology and anthropology, and zoology. Many have gained higher education places at prestigious institutions such as University College London, King's College London, Queen Mary's, York, Bristol, and Southampton, while others have secured competitive apprenticeships and direct entry into the workforce.
Central to the school's ethos is the core value of resilience. Over the course of their studies, students have shown impressive determination and adaptability, working diligently through the challenges of A-level qualifications to reach their personal goals.
Mrs MacInnes, Principal at Baylis Court School, said: "Today is about celebrating the individual journeys of our students and acknowledging the quiet determination they have shown over the last two years. Supported by our dedicated staff and supportive families, they have worked consistently to achieve their results. True to our mission of inspiring leaders of tomorrow, we are proud not just of what they have achieved academically, but of the kind, inquisitive, and well-rounded young people they have become."
As students prepare to take their next steps, everyone at Baylis Court School wishes the Class of 2026 the very best for the future.

pageCache.pageTitle: GCSE Results Day - GCSE Results Day - Latest News - Baylis Court School
pageCache.text:
GCSE Results Day
Pupils and staff at Baylis Court School came together today to mark GCSE results day, celebrating the hard work, perseverance, and personal achievements of this year’s Year 11 cohort.
The school’s mission, ‘Inspiring Leaders of Tomorrow’ underpins everything at Baylis Court. Pupils are expected, encouraged and supported to achieve their very best academically. The results mark the culmination of years of dedication, with pupils successfully securing their chosen next steps across a range of post-16 pathways, including A-levels and vocational courses. Many are now set to progress into the Sixth Form at Baylis Court, or in local schools and colleges, equipped with the strong foundations needed for future success. All Year 11 pupils should be rightly proud of their achievements.
Mrs MacInnes, Principal at Baylis Court said "We are absolutely thrilled to celebrate these fantastic grades with our pupils today. These results are a testament to the immense hard work, dedication, and resilience shown by both our Year 11s and our exceptional staff. Behind every grade is a story of commitment, and we are immensely proud of what this group of fabulous young women have achieved."
Central to the school's ethos is the core value of resilience. Over the course of their secondary studies, pupils have shown impressive determination and adaptability, working diligently through the challenges of their GCSE courses to reach their personal goals.
As students prepare to take their next steps into Key Stage 5 and beyond, everyone at Baylis Court School wishes the GCSE Class of 2026 the very best for the future and looks forward to welcoming many of them back in September for A-level studies.

Special Educational Needs and Disability (SEND)
At Baylis Court School we welcome all students including those who have special educational needs or disabilities (SEND). We encourage high expectations of everyone in our school community and work hard to support one another in achieving these goals. Our Special Educational Needs and Disabilities Co-ordinator (SENDCO) is Ms Ru Rees.
The promotion of progress and achievement of individual students is founded on the belief that:
The school seeks to raise achievement and remove barriers to learning on the mutual understanding that SEND is a whole school matter; that all teachers are teachers of children with SEND.
Our SENDCO is Ms R Rees. You can contact her via email RRS@bayliscourt.slough.sch.uk

Our Aim
The overall aim of the careers provision at Baylis Court School is to provide effective and impartial careers education and guidance to enable our students to manage their own career development successfully, by helping them to acquire the skills, attitudes and abilities they will need to move through life with confidence. This is delivered in a variety of ways, not only through the Careers programme, but embedded in the teaching and learning throughout their school life.

pageCache.pageTitle: More details about staff benefits - Baylis Court School
pageCache.text:
More details about staff benefits
Benefits in more detail
Competitive salaries
We offer competitive pay for teaching and support staff, aligned to the role and level of responsibility. Starting salary is based on your role’s pay range, your experience and market conditions—so your skills and background are recognised from day one.
National terms and conditions
We are committed to national terms and conditions for our workforce:
This provides clarity, fairness and consistency across the Trust.
Support staff: NJC Green Book
Pension scheme
All contracted staff are automatically enrolled in either:
Teachers’ Pension Scheme (TPS), or
Local Government Pension Scheme (LGPS) (as applicable).
Parking support
We aim to make commuting as straightforward as possible. Free on-site parking is available at many of our schools. Where on-street parking permits are required, these are fully funded by the Trust. (At Battle Primary Academy, on-site parking is limited and not available for all staff.)
Tools and support to do your job well
We want every colleague to have the tools they need to work effectively:
Advice and counselling (Employee Assistance Programme)
Support is available whenever you need it. Our Employee Assistance Programme provides:
Healthcare Cash Plan: Medicash Healthcare Cash Plan
All staff have access to a Medicash Healthcare Cash Plan, helping you claim money back on everyday healthcare costs (up to annual limits), including:
Dental treatment
Eye tests
Complementary therapies (e.g., acupuncture, osteopathy, chiropractic treatment)
Chiropody/podiatry
Free Eye tests and DSE glasses contribution
We’re committed to protecting the health, safety and wellbeing of our staff. If you’re a DSE user and request an eye test, the Trust will fund it. Where the test confirms you need glasses specifically for DSE work, we’ll contribute up to £49 towards the cost.
UpLearn: 50% off online courses
TLT staff can access 50% off UpLearn courses in selected subjects, including:
To take advantage of this offer, please mention Thames Learning Trust when purchasing course(s) from UpLearn. UpLearn also advertises a guarantee of A/A* at A level (or your money back), subject to their terms.
UpLearn website: uplearn.co.uk
GCSE: Chemistry
Lifestyle benefits and discounts (Wider Wallet & Wider Fitness)
Save money with the Wider Wallet portal, offering discounts at hundreds of retailers, including supermarkets, plus offers on health and lifestyle activities such as gym memberships and family days out.
Cycle to Work scheme
Our Cycle to Work scheme helps you spread the cost of a new bike and cycling equipment through salary sacrifice, saving on tax and National Insurance.
